newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Nov 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has suggested to President Shahabuddin Ahmed that he could make an independent probe into main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party's (BNP) allegation of harassment of political opponents.
A bill was placed in parliament on Wednesday to reorganise Bangladesh Commerce and Investment Ltd (BCI), a non-banking financial institution, into a bank for the interest of its depositors.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has underscored the need for optimum use of modern communication technology in the country, saying it is imperative to face the challenges of the new century.
The Prime Minister has meanwhile asked the BNP not to embark on any suicidal programmes that might damage the congenial investment atmosphere and scare away investors.

In a sudden development that almost paralysed the Dhaka Stock Exchange, the members of the bourse were gheraoed by unauthorised kerb market operators throughout Wednesday, prompting police to baton charge and use teargas.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has urged opposition BNP members to return to parliament soon as the legislature prorogued its Autumn session late on Wednesday.

Bangladesh is observing the Armed Forces Day on Thursday with due solemnity and enthusiasm. The prime Minister and the President, in separate statements, have recalled the glorious, heroic role of the armed forces during the 1971 liberation war.
The government has taken a massive programme for generating a total of 2,600 megawatt electricity in next five years, besides modernising and infusing dynamism in the entire power sector.
The government intends to formulate a broad-based telecom policy aiming to end the long-standing state monopoly and promote competition to ensure better service.
